articles.title: In 1998, George Clooney was DELETED from 'The Thin Red Line' almost entirely; decades later, he shares how that experience changed his perspective towards the industry
articles.summary: At the Venice Film Festival, George Clooney discusses his experience filming 'The Thin Red Line' and how being cut from most scenes reshaped his perspective on directing.
articles.body: While George Clooney has faced much success in his career, there have been times when his hard work did not always pay off. The beloved actor recently attended the Venice Film Festival, where he received the Golden Lion award for lifetime achievement. During one segment of the festival, the actor looked back on one of his most famous works, ‘The Thin Red Line,' a war film released in 1998.George Clooney revisits his days filming for ‘The Thin Red Line'On September 3, Clooney attended a moderated conversation at the Venice Film Festival, where he was asked what he enjoys about directing rather than just acting. PEOPLE reported that, while answering the question, the actor said he has much more control over a film as a director than he did as an actor.While answering the question, he recalled his time filming for ‘The Thin Red Line.' He shared that while filming the movie, he did many scenes; however, most never made it to the final theatrical cut. He shared, “I remember I did Thin Red Line, which is this really interesting film, and Terry Malick was coming back; he hadn’t worked in 15 years and wanted to come back and do a film, so I thought, ‘I’m going to help him get this film made, and I’m going to do this part for him.’”Further on, he explained that he had shot for the film in Australia for months, adding, “He cut me completely out except for the last scene in the film. The very last scene. I watched it, and I was like, ‘He cut me completely out. Am I only in the last scene? My God, I look like an a**hole!' And he said, ‘No, George, it’s pretty fun,’ and I said, ‘Oh, s***’ So you can really change people’s performances. The director is in charge; the director is the painter.”About ‘The Thin Red Line’The war film is set during the Second World War and focuses on a troupe of US soldiers who fight on a Pacific island, specifically the Battle of Guadalcanal. Along with Clooney, the film starred many other big names, including Sean Penn, Adrien Brody, Jim Caviezel, John Cusack, Woody Harrelson, Jared Leto, Tim Blake Nelson, Nick Nolte, John C. Reilly, and John Travolta. ‘The Thin Red Line’ was based on James Jones's 1962 autobiographical novel about the World War II battle for Guadalcanal. The film was released in 1998 and was directed by Terrence Malick. The film marked his return to the filmmaking industry after an almost 20-year hiatus.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: Janhvi Kapoor personality rights case: Delhi HC appoints Gautam Bhatia as amicus curiae; 552 URLs ordered to be removed
articles.summary: The Delhi High Court is examining the legal limits of personality rights in the digital space. The matter has come up in actor Janhvi Kapoor's petitio.
articles.body: The Delhi High Court is examining the legal limits of personality rights in the digital space. The matter has come up in actor Janhvi Kapoor's petition against the alleged unauthorised use of her identity online. The court has now brought in independent legal assistance to examine the wider issues involved. Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani appointed advocate Gautam Bhatia as amicus curiae in Janhvi Kapoor's case on September 3, as reported by LiveLaw.Delhi High Court appoints amicus curiaeReportedly, advocate Gautam Bhatia will assist the Delhi High Court in examining the questions arising from Janhvi Kapoor's personality rights plea. The case involves the alleged misuse of the actor's name, image and likeness on the internet. A similar arrangement has been made in another matter involving actor Vivek Oberoi. Advocate Rohan Alva has been appointed as amicus curiae in Oberoi's personality rights case. The two proceedings involve broader questions about the protection available to public figures online. They also require the court to consider how such rights interact with legitimate digital expression.Janhvi Kapoor seeks protection from online misuseJanhvi Kapoor's petition raises concerns over several forms of alleged unauthorised use of her identity. The material mentioned in the plea includes sexually explicit and vulgar content. The petition also covers alleged impersonation. Commercial exploitation of the actor's name and likeness is another issue before the court. The dispute involves thousands of online links. Janhvi Kapoor had identified 6,884 URLs as part of her plea. However, the court did not accept a request for a blanket direction covering every URL. Instead, the links are being examined according to the nature of the material involved. This approach allows different types of content to be considered separately.Court directs removal of 552 URLsThe Delhi High Court previously ordered the removal of 552 URLs. These links were prima facie found to contain grossly sexually vulgar or pornographic material. The other URLs are being divided into different categories. One category covers sexually vulgar content. Another concerns material that directly generates revenue through the alleged exploitation of Janhvi Kapoor's personality rights. The classification also includes links that indirectly use her name or likeness to promote merchandise or services. The categorisation is significant because not every online reference to a celebrity necessarily carries the same legal implications. The court is therefore examining the nature and purpose of the individual content.Janhvi Kapoor's legal team seeks interim reliefAt Thursday's hearing, Janhvi Kapoor's lawyers informed the court that the URLs had been classified as directed. Her counsel then sought an early hearing for the application seeking interim relief. The request comes as the court continues to consider how the different categories of links should be dealt with. The proceedings could also help clarify the scope of personality rights in cases involving large-scale online content. The issue extends beyond Janhvi Kapoor's individual complaint.Janhvi Kapoor's last released film was the Telugu action drama 'Peddi'. The film arrived in theatres on June 4, 2026.Disclaimer: The information in this report is based on a legal hearing as reported by a third-party source. articles.title: Rowan Atkinson to honour inspiration for Mr Bean at Purbeck Film Festival
articles.summary: The actor is set to appear at the festival that hosts events across Dorset from 16 October to 1 November.
articles.body:
Actor Rowan Atkinson will join one of UK's longest-running rural film festivals for an event honouring a French comic genius who inspired Mr Bean.

From 16 October to 1 November, the Purbeck Film Festival, which was founded in 1996, will run screenings and events in Corfe Castle, village halls, secret gardens, restaurants and stately homes across Dorset.

One of them is a Jacques Tati day at The Mowlem theatre in Swanage - Atkinson has credited the Academy Award filmmaker, actor and mime as an inspiration for his iconic comic character.

Festival organisers said that exclusive previews, Cannes prize-winners, UK premieres and local stories were also part of its 30th anniversary programme.

Since its inception, the festival has grown beyond its modest first year with 1,700 visitors across 21 screenings.

It has featured guests over the years include The Queen director Stephen Frears, cinematographer Jack Cardiff and actress Dame Maggie Smith.

The festival said that patrons, actor and playwright Sir Mark Rylance and filmmaker Sir Sam Mendes, "continue a legacy built on rural roots and quiet ambition".

Reflecting on the milestone, Sir Mark called the anniversary "quite remarkable" , adding that small festivals like Purbeck are a "godsend for filmmakers" that help nurture the human heart of cinema.

One attendee praised the variety of venues and said they were seeing films "which I would probably not see at a traditional cinema".

This year's edition will also see BAFTA-winning director Philippa Lowthorpe presenting her adaptation H Is for Hawk, starring Claire Foy at St Mary's Church in Swanage.

Festival director Claire Burns said it had "always belonged to the communities of Purbeck and the audiences who travel from across the country to be part of something truly special".

articles.title: Descubren una isla flotante en Canadá, desaparece misteriosamente de las imágenes por satélite, pero al tiempo vuelve a aparecer
articles.standfirst: Una pareja de navegantes descubrió esta nueva isla en la Columbia Británica
articles.summary: Una pareja de navegantes descubrió esta nueva isla en la Columbia Británica
articles.body: La naturaleza nos muestra cada día que tiene cosas inexplicables, que por mucho que se estudien, nos seguirá sorprendiendo como si fuéramos niños toda la vida. Una estas maravillas de la vida y del medio ambiente se ha vivido en la Columbia Británica. En el lago de Wlliston, el de agua dulce más grande de la Columbia Británica, apareció una isla flotante de 9800 metros cuadrados, equivalente a un campo y medio de fútbol. Una pareja de navegantes grabó la escena. Poco después, una imagen de satélite confirmó su existencia. Para sorpresa de todos, pocas semanas después, la isla desapareció, literalmente, del mapa. Se había esfumado. Nadie daba crédito y las autoridades comenzaron una búsqueda que dio resultado, aunque en otra zona del embalse. Fue un portavoz de BC Hydro, la empresa pública encargada del mantenimiento del embalse y de una presa cercana, quien descubrió la existencia de la isla tras ver un vídeo que circulaba por las redes sociales. “Pensé: ‘Bueno, podría ser cualquier lugar’”, dijo Bob Gammer a la BBC, y agregó que inicialmente creyó que el video había sido generado por inteligencia artificial. “Quizás no sea real”. Según explicó Gammer, la isla parece haber sido simplemente arrastrada hacia la costa y encallado a unos 30 km del lugar donde fue avistada por primera vez. Para él, la teoría más lógica en este misterioso caso es que probablemente se formó a lo largo de los años a partir de la acumulación de madera flotante que sirvió de soporte para que las plantas y los árboles echaran raíces. Gammer confesó también que en un principio creyó que la isla había desaparecido porque este año, tras muchos años con apenas lluvia, el nivel del agua del embalse había subido y alcanzaron un máximo que no se veía desde 2012.

articles.title: In 1993, Tim Curry bought Seyler House for USD 650,000 when it was on the brink of DEMOLITION, but he saved it and turned it into a Mediterranean dream house; now it's been sold for USD 7.5 million
articles.summary: Explore the incredible journey of Tim Curry's Seyler House, a stunning Mediterranean villa in Los Feliz, bought for $650,000 and recently sold for $7.5 million. Discover the history, unique architectural features, and its transformation by the beloved actor.
articles.body: Over the years, Tim Curry has owned quite a lot of properties; however, his Los Feliz home in LA is perhaps one of his most iconic and legendary ones. The beloved ‘The Rocky Horror Picture Show’ actor bought the home back in 1993. The 1922 Spanish Colonial Revival/Mediterranean villa, located at 2666 Aberdeen Avenue in the Los Feliz neighbourhood of Los Angeles, was on the cusp of being demolished. However, Curry ended up buying it out at the last minute and spent years making the old house into a Mediterranean dream house.How did Tim Curry land his LA home?Architectural Digest reported that Curry bought the house for USD 650,000 in 1993 just when it was about to be demolished for a new property. In a 1998 feature with the outlet, the actor had laid bare how his home came to be. Curry often reflected on how the people and places around him inspired his taste in many things, which also included his home.When Curry moves to Hollywood for better opportunities, he and his friend, Annie Potts, set out to cruise the market and see what's available in the real estate market at the time. The two visited a house in Los Feliz that had just come on the market. It was Potts's favourite; however, it had been painted a bright tomato orange and was about to be demolished.However, Curry fell in love at first sight when he went inside the property, feeling as if he had been transported all the way to Ecuador. He put in his offer right away and was just in luck since the previous owner had backed out of the deal. He shared at the time, “I soon learned that the previous bidder had been told by her psychic that the house was haunted and had just withdrawn from escrow.” The mansion is known as the Seyler House.History of Tim Curry’s Seyler HouseCurry’s LA home had quite a bit of history behind it. The home was built in 1922 and was built and designed by architect Stiles Clements. He was a well-known name who was responsible for a lot of public buildings in Los Angeles. The design of the home was directly inspired by the Spanish Colonial Revival. As to why the house appealed to Curry so much, the actor shared, “It has none of those elements one sees so often: festivals of wrought iron, little Juliet balconies, and guitars strumming in every corner.”More about Tim Curry’s Seyler HouseCurry’s home is an embodiment of the Mediterranean region, with old-school thick stucco walls, arched doorways filling the entire home, deep recesses, and red-tile roofs; the home was love at first sight for the beloved actor. The entire home is covered in rustic brown-toned walls, along with black-and-white checkered flooring and cosy carpets. The property spans 4,000 square feet, containing 4 bedrooms and 3.5 bathrooms. It also features stained-glass windows, vintage tile, and exposed wood-beam ceilings.Curry also drew his inspiration from an Irish estate owned by the Guinness family, where he was invited to stay for a while. While talking about the same, he shared, “It was the most beautiful and comfortable house I’d ever been to. The dining room’s red Chinese silk walls had been blasted by the sun and were covered with faded Hokusai and Hiroshige prints bound the way they used to be in the 19th century, in black passe-partout. We sat at the end of an enormous Regency table and ate potato pie.”Curry further shared that he loved the maximalist aspect of the home, adding, “There was an extraordinary range of paintings and just the sort of patina—and obsessions—of several centuries of people who’d lived there, with everything having a layer of dog over it. A great jumble it was, all arranged by an eye.”Tim Curry sold the house in 2000 for USD 2.6 million, and it has now been sold for USD 7.5 millionIn 2000, Curry sold the beautiful home for USD 2.6 million, and it was later owned by a series of celebrities. This included names like Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, Noah Wyle, Robert Pattinson, Jim Parsons, and Aaron Paul. The house had been on the market for some time now, though, according to reports shared online by a realtor, the home’s contract was cleared with a pending buyer. The news of the sale came only hours after the actor passed away. The property was originally listed for sale in June for USD 10.4 million. articles.title: How Dolly Parton used her authentic country wit to beat Hollywood critics to the punchline
articles.summary: Dolly Parton's self-deprecating wit and comedic genius helped her shatter country music stereotypes and conquer Hollywood, colleagues recall.
articles.body: Long before Dolly Parton became a global superstar, she mastered the art of beating others to the punch line, making her humor nearly as recognizable as her country music. Following the country icon’s death at age 80, directors, country legends and media experts recalled how Parton built a down-home comedic persona that helped her break stereotypes and find success in Hollywood without abandoning her roots. As fans mourn the loss of a cultural icon, those who worked with Parton remember a professional known for her self-deprecating wit. Parton, best known for her legendary country music career, also appeared in several comedy films, including "9 to 5" and the romantic comedy "Straight Talk." She also hosted the country-variety show "Dolly," which debuted in Sept. 1976 and aired for one season. Another series bearing her name followed in the 1980s. DOLLY PARTON'S LIFE IN HER OWN WORDS: FROM SMOKY MOUNTAINS POVERTY TO COUNTRY MUSIC IMMORTALITY By then, Parton was no newcomer to comedy and variety television. She appeared on "The Porter Wagoner Show" from 1967 to 1974, where she spent years refining her comedic persona and quick wit. As a young performer from Sevierville, Tennessee, Parton entered a Nashville country music scene where larger-than-life comedy was already a tradition. Country Music Hall of Famer Ray Stevens, the two-time Grammy winner behind novelty hits including "The Streak," worked with Parton on some of her early recordings in Nashville. He told Fox News Digital that the young Parton he met was far different from the international icon she later became. STEVE DOOCY: THE DOLLY PARTON I SAW WHEN THE CAMERAS STOPPED ROLLING "The young 19 or 20-year-old Dolly Parton I met in 1965, when she first came to Nashville and I produced her first recordings, was not the internationally known Dolly Parton we just lost," Stevens told Fox News Digital. "Young Dolly from Sevierville, TN, had not yet created and perfected the persona we all loved." Stevens worked with Parton on early recordings, including "Busy Signal" and "I’ve Known You All My Life." He also appeared with Parton in comedy sketches on "Dolly," and said she understood the larger-than-life tradition of country comedy. "All country comedians have always been outrageous characters, like Speck Rhodes and his wild suits, or Minnie Pearl in her hat with the price tag still hanging down and her loud ‘Howdy,’" Stevens said. "Dolly also liked to laugh and make other people laugh, and she knew her audience because she grew up making the people around her laugh. She knew what they found funny because she found it funny too, so her comedy was authentic," he added. DOLLY PARTON REFUSED TO PICK POLITICAL SIDES FOR DECADES: ‘I’M NOT IN POLITICS, I’M AN ENTERTAINER’ Stevens said Parton also found humor in her own larger-than-life image. "Dolly's secret is that she thought the Dolly with the big hair, big personality, and other big assets was funny. She was outrageously dressed and endowed and liable to say anything," he said. Stevens said the contrast between Parton’s larger-than-life image and her thoughtful songwriting helped make her "one-of-a-kind." That Nashville persona eventually followed Parton into Hollywood. DOLLY PARTON’S SIX-DECADE LOVE STORY WITH CARL DEAN BEGAN AT A LAUNDROMAT In the 1992 romantic comedy "Straight Talk," Parton played an upbeat small-town woman who moves to Chicago and accidentally becomes an on-air radio advice host named "Doctor Shirlee." Director Barnet Kellman said Parton understood exactly how to use her public persona for comedy. "To say Dolly was in on the joke doesn’t begin to cover it," Kellman told Fox News Digital. "She designed the joke." "She was super-intelligent and could explain to you everything about the ‘Dolly Parton character,’ why her costume and makeup and hair and figure had the effect on people that they did," he said. Kellman said Parton was always willing to try new things, "as long as it didn’t require taking off the high heels," and noted that she knew what made her character funny and how to "deploy her magic." DOLLY PARTON LAID TO REST AS NIECE SHARES EMOTIONAL TRIBUTE TO ‘GRANNY’ "She was a terrific comic writer and gave me pages and pages of down-home truisms that were — at the end of the day — just good advice and precepts that Dolly herself lived by. We used those comebacks as answers to the questions the callers to her radio advice show would ask," Kellman added. "Straight Talk" was part of a larger film career that included classics like "Rhinestone," "Joyful Noise," and "Steel Magnolias." Kellman said that on set, Parton often had an "openness as a scene partner" and never approached anyone with judgment. "She turned cynical men into adoring puppies," he said. "The Dolly that came to work was a committed professional — she came in character and stayed in character — she was the character — yet somehow that ‘Dolly character’ she’d crafted was authentically who she was. That’s what made her so exceptional," he added. While her films expanded her Hollywood career, television helped Parton reach an even broader audience. Jason Lynch, curator at the Paley Center for Media, said Parton used television appearances, from award shows to talk shows, to reach audiences far beyond country music. "One major reason that Dolly enjoyed the degree of crossover success that eluded so many other country artists was her mastery at using her varied television appearances to build her appeal with audiences," Lynch told Fox News Digital. "And by showcasing her comic sensibility and sharp wit, she managed to even win over audiences that weren’t country music fans." CARRIE UNDERWOOD HONORS DOLLY PARTON'S FAITH AND LEGACY DURING EMOTIONAL CONCERT TRIBUTE Lynch pointed out that Parton strategically used self-deprecation to control her own narrative. "One of Dolly’s greatest tools was her use of self-deprecating humor — she knew all the jokes that people could make about her chest and her upbringing, so she made them first," Lynch said. "In doing so, she was able to dismantle and rise above so many of the stereotypes that existed about country artists like her." DOLLY PARTON SLEPT AS LITTLE AS 3 HOURS, DID HER OWN HAIR AND MAKEUP ON SET, CO-STAR DANICA MCKELLAR SAYS He said the "universal adoration" Parton received across generations and political divides made her a unique kind of celebrity. "And she smartly connected with audiences by popping up on a variety of beloved shows over the decades, including ‘The Simpsons,’ ‘Reba,’ ‘Designing Women,’ and most recently, the series finale of ‘Grace and Frankie,’ where she reunited with her ‘9 to 5’ costars Jane Fonda and Lily Tomlin," Lynch added. Her television reach also extended to younger generations through her recurring role on Disney Channel's "Hannah Montana," where she played Aunt Dolly alongside her real-life goddaughter, Miley Cyrus. "But the TV show role that might have had the most seismic impact in endearing her to a new generation of fans was ‘Hannah Montana,’ when she played Aunt Dolly to her real-life goddaughter, Miley Cyrus. Suddenly, a generation who wasn’t even born when ‘Jolene’ or ‘9 to 5’ came out was able to discover and fall for her, just like audiences had done decades earlier," Lynch said. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Whether it was her ‘Tonight Show with Johnny Carson’ appearances — which dominated social media feeds this week after her passing — her two variety shows she hosted, teaming up with other legends like Carol Burnett and Kenny Rogers, the TV movies she produced in the 2010s — like Dolly Parton’s ‘Coat of Many Colors’ — or her unforgettable turns in shows like ‘Hannah Montana,’ Dolly was one of the most cherished TV personalities of all time," he added.

articles.title: La atrevida aparición de Sydney Sweeney en el Festival de Venecia que cumple con sus 'provocaciones'
articles.standfirst: La actriz es conocida por sus impactantes estilismos que los tiene ya interiorizados
articles.summary: La actriz es conocida por sus impactantes estilismos que los tiene ya interiorizados
articles.body: Sydney Sweeney no deja a nadie neutro. La actriz ha sido una de las más aclamadas en el Festival de Venecia y al margen de sus dotes para la interpretación su puesta en escena siempre guarda alguna sorpresa. Lo ha vuelto a hacer. Todo el mundo ha hablado de ella. Todo el mundo se ha centrado en ella. Su forma de vestir ha causado furor entre los presentes por el modelito que ha utilizado. La actriz posó en el photocall de la fiesta que dio Armani Beauty en el Festival. En cuanto Sweeney pisó la alfombra roja, todos los flashes se posaron en ella, sorprendiendo con un diseño plateado que lo puso en el top de apariciones más polémicas, como la de la gala Variety's 2025 Power of Women. De hecho, la artista norteamericana lució un conjunto de la marca Giorgio Armani, que pertenece a la colección otoño-invierno 2000/01 de la firma. Un diseño que es trasparente con lentejuelas plateadas, un escote redondo y una flor negra en uno de los tirantes. Esto provocaba un efecto transparente que dejaba a a la vista su ropa interior. Sweeney no había pisado la alfombra roja oficial del Festival de Venecia hasta el momento, circunstancia que no sucede desde su debut en el 2022, cuando acudió a la premier de 'Bones and All', donde posó junto a su compañera de reparto de Euphoria, Maude Apatow. Sydney ha cumplido con la norma. Porque en el festival, los invitados tienen una libertad total a la hora de vestir, con una alfombra roja que deja tendencias. En esta ocasión como el vestido homenaje a Marilyn Monroe de Ana de Armas, el look de pedrería de Dakota Johnson o el diseño con efecto mojado de Zendaya. Pero Sweeney va más allá que es como habitúa.
